A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of maximal update parameterization for predictive coding and target propagation. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and simulation results on FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and synthetic data, including hyperparameter transfer, gradient alignment, and activation dynamics.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CNN results on CIFAR-100 in Figure S.13.

M1.justification: The PC and TP/DTP procedures and principal parameterization rules remain unchanged, including Table 1. Expanded algorithm descriptions and corrections to derivations do not establish a changed training method.

E1.justification: Figure S.13 adds CIFAR-100 image classification with a CNN. FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and synthetic-data coverage are retained; CIFAR-10 was already identified in v1's accompanying appendix discussion.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their SP/NTK parameterization comparisons and BP/GN gradient comparisons. The new CIFAR-100 panel uses the existing comparator set; additional related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Figure S.12 changes the stated base width from 1 to 128 while retaining its curves. Figure S.13 reduces the reported CIFAR-10 width sweep's maximum from 16384 to 8192. These are reported setting changes, without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure S.13 extends the analysis of accuracy versus width to CIFAR-100 and revises the CIFAR-10 scaling evidence. Existing analyses of initialization, inference iterations, base width, loss, optimizer, and feedback learning remain; the TP activation-dynamics analysis is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or an uncertainty-reporting procedure. The revised results introduce no such reporting.

E6.justification: Figure S.13 adds CIFAR-100 accuracy curves and revises CIFAR-10 values, including SP collapsing at smaller displayed widths. Its VGG/FashionMNIST results remain unchanged. Most other plots retain their results after accounting for relocation and display changes; the revised curves do not establish a controlled performance improvement.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit proof of the existing Corollary 4.3 in Appendix B.2.2, corrects the width exponent of the feedback term in Section 4.3, and revises indices and derivative factors in the TP derivation. The principal theorem conclusions and parameterization exponents are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: PC/TP parameterizations enabling hyperparameter transfer, parameterization-dependent PC gradients, and the disappearance of TP's kernel regime under the analyzed conditions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a mechanism explanation linking larger output-layer inference steps to downward error propagation and GN-like behavior. Appendix A.1 adds expectations of applicability to auxiliary-coordinate, ADMM, and alternating-minimization methods. The existing one-step and linear-network limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1.3 and E newly specify that experimental feedback networks use the forward network's activation function, distinguishing these experiments from the linear-feedback theorem. Conversely, Figure 2 drops some fixed-dimension settings previously printed above its panels. Most training-recipe details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The new extended related-work discussion substantially expands connections to learning-rate transfer and scaling-law research, PC's probabilistic origins, TP's biological motivations, and other local optimization methods. It adds works such as Noci et al., Qiu et al., Friston, and the MAC/ADMM/alternating-minimization literature.

P1.justification: v2 substantially expands background explanations and reorganizes the former combined derivation appendix into background, PC, and TP sections. It relocates algorithm and nudged-PC introductions, revises the main-text explanation of stable parameterization, and makes numerous terminology and language corrections.

P2.justification: v2 adds an abbreviation table, expands Table 1's labels, corrects Figure 2's panel descriptions, revises several axes and captions, and adds a CIFAR-100 panel to Figure S.13. v1 Figure 6 moves to Figure S.14. Conference formatting changes the layout, but most graphical displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added proof of Corollary 4.3, corrected scaling expression, expanded background, and explicit feedback activations improve clarity and assessability. CIFAR-100 provides limited additional empirical support. Some Figure 2 settings disappear, and the revised CIFAR-10 curves lack an explanation, limiting reproducibility gains. Overall, v2 usefully refines the existing paper without substantially changing its scientific foundation.
